source.excerpt: Ride the storm and direct the whirlwind.
trail: The fetched Liberty Fund anthology reproduces the phrase in Objections and Answers Respecting the Administration. The surrounding sentence describes a demagogue who would create disorder for personal power. Wikiquote supplies the same source; the phrase is genuine but detached imperatives can reverse its force. author.heading: About Alexander Hamilton
author.bio: Hamilton was a Federalist statesman and Treasury secretary. His private political memoranda could be sharply critical of rivals and of leaders he believed might exploit instability.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Hamilton used the image in a warning about a dangerous political leader who could profit from disorder. Turning the phrase into a free-standing command reverses the force of its original setting: it describes a feared capability rather than advice to the reader.
